prior_importants.description: A test the branch deletes is asked whether the branch's own config collects it, so deleting a test suite together with its `include` entry counts the deleted lines as source and can trip the 600-line flag on a harmless change.

testInputsIntact checks only the root run inputs and node_modules links against the pinned sha, never the collected test files. The branch's own build script runs in the writable gate checkout before the suites, so it can delete or rewrite a collected `src/big.test.ts`. Vitest then never runs the committed file and the test stage passes. The split reads collection from the sha's tree, so it still counts the committed 2000 lines as test.

`testInputsIntact` treats the test run's inputs as clean after the build, but the package manager that runs the test script comes from the corepack install in the per-repo toolchain cache. The build child is granted write access there (sandbox.utils.ts:413), and the unsandboxed session can write there too. A build that swaps corepack's pnpm or yarn entrypoint makes the test stage run the branch's package manager, and neither check looks at it.

The branch's root package.json is never compared across sides, so a branch can name itself `vitest` with an `exports` map, which (assuming vite's resolver checks self-references first) points the shared config's `import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config'` at a branch module that vitest runs.

findings.description: testInputsIntact is checked only after the build and before the split, so a failed root test stage's first run can narrow vitest.config.ts, the re-run loads the narrowed config and restores it, both checks pass, and an uncollected production file counts as test.

`foldsOntoAnother` only catches siblings that differ by ASCII case, because it compares names with `toLowerCase()`. A non-ASCII sibling that APFS folds onto an ASCII test path, such as `src/big.teſt.ts` next to `src/big.test.ts`, is not caught. The gate's checkout then writes both blobs to one file, so the ASCII path still counts as a collected test even though its blob never reaches the disk.

pnpm loads the root `.pnpmfile.cjs` while it reads its config for every command, `run` included. The code doesn't list that file anywhere: it is not in `VITEST_RUN_INPUT`, `PACKAGE_MANAGER_CONFIG` or `PNP_RUNTIME`, and the `pnpmfile` key is not in `RUNS_A_FILE`. So a branch that commits one, or a build that writes one, runs its own code in the test script's pnpm process. Both checks still pass and both sides still collect.

`RUNS_A_FILE` matches the raw text of the package-manager configs. npm and pnpm read `.npmrc` with `ini`, which `JSON.parse`s a quoted key, so `"node-options"=--import ./scripts/reg.mjs` is read as `node-options` but never matches the regex. Once a shared `.npmrc` holds that line, the branch's `scripts/reg.mjs` loads into the vitest run while both sides still collect.

VITEST_UNREAD_TEST_KEYS omits `test.passWithNoTests`. Vitest's runner only fails a collected file with no tests when that option is unset, so in a repo whose config sets it, a collected `*.test.ts` holding only production code passes the test stage and counts as test.

process_issues.description: review-consolidator (haiku) failed with API 403 (Cloudflare authentication_failed); dedup done inline. The five findings had five distinct root causes, so nothing was merged.

All review-validator calls (5 in parallel, then 1 retry, opus) failed with API 403 (Cloudflare authentication_failed), so none of the 5 important findings was validated. Rather than post unvalidated inline comments, the orchestrator downgraded all five to nit under §6 'tag must match body'. ADR 0143 L180-184 explicitly accepts that a collected file holding production code passes the test stage ('The branch can reach the same count more cheaply by putting one trivial test in that file, which collection already takes for test code'). Every finding (test re-run narrowing the config, non-ASCII APFS fold sibling, .pnpmfile.cjs, escaped .npmrc keys, passWithNoTests) reaches only that accepted outcome for the diff-size split. The .pnpmfile.cjs vector also zeroes the test stage's exit gate-wide, which predates this PR. A re-run with working validators could re-tag them.

Round 6 budget (REVIEW.md §1): only correctness (2), security (2) and guards were spawned. conventions, docs, context, simplicity and maintainability were skipped for the round budget. spec was skipped because there is no closing issue or spec source, and workflow-safety because no workflow changed. Since the prior reviewed head 03ef794, only merge-gate.service.ts and its test changed, through the main merge 67d6d66, which correctness confirmed left the PR's hunks intact. All four owed importants are untouched in code and carried as unresolved.
The guards reviewer's git diff over the three main source files was truncated at 36.9 KB, so it judged those files partly by import lists and Grep. No guard tripped.
